sentences.text: This ancient fish possessed a large, toothed rostrum that closely resembled that of a modern sawfish.
Fossils of Ischyrhiza have been discovered in Canada, the United States, Mexico, Uzbekistan, Japan, Niger, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.
Ischyrhiza is classified within the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish like sharks and rays.
It belongs to the family Sclerorhynchidae.
The genus Ischyrhiza was first described by Leidy in 1856.
The type species of the genus Ischyrhiza is Ischyrhiza mira, the specimen the species is based on.
The genus was originally placed under the authority of Cope in 1875.
The time range for Ischyrhiza spans from the Albian to the Thanetian, approximately 113.2 to 56 million years ago.
Ischyrhiza lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically from the Cenomanian to Maastrichtian stages.

Phylogenetic analyses suggest that Ischyrhiza, along with Schizorhiza and Onchopristis, forms a distinct clade closer to the extant family Rajidae (true skates), which may render the suborder Sclerorhynchoidei paraphyletic.
